media.name: Oil paint
media.description: Pigment ground into drying oil. It dries slowly, so artists can blend colors and rework a surface for days.
media.history: Oil painting spread across Europe in the 1400s and became the dominant medium for painters for centuries.

media.name: Acrylic paint
media.description: Pigment suspended in a water-based polymer. It dries fast, can be thinned with water, and works on many surfaces.
media.history: Acrylic paints were developed in the 1900s and were widely adopted by artists in the mid-1900s.

media.name: Watercolor
media.description: Transparent pigment mixed with water and applied to paper. Light shows through the layers, giving a luminous look.
media.history: Watercolor has been used for thousands of years, from Egyptian manuscripts to landscape painters of the 1700s and 1800s.

media.name: Graffiti
media.description: Paint, markers and other tools used to mark public surfaces such as walls and trains.
media.history: Writing on walls is ancient, and modern graffiti grew out of urban street culture in the late 1900s.

media.name: Stone
media.description: Carved by removing material from marble, limestone or granite. Mistakes are hard to undo, so the sculptor plans carefully.
media.history: Stone carving is among the oldest sculptural traditions and appears in nearly every ancient civilization.

media.name: Bronze
media.description: A metal alloy usually poured into a mold. It allows fine detail and can support thin, outstretched poses.
media.history: Bronze casting developed in the ancient world and was refined in places such as Greece, China and West Africa.

media.name: Ceramics
media.description: Clay shaped by hand or on a wheel, then hardened by firing in a kiln. Glazes add color and a waterproof surface.
media.history: Fired clay objects date back tens of thousands of years and are found in cultures worldwide.

media.name: Wood
media.description: Carved, joined or assembled. The grain of the wood guides how the sculptor works.
media.history: Wood carving has been used for ritual objects, architecture and figures across many cultures, though wood decays more easily than stone or metal.

media.name: Weaving
media.description: Interlacing lengthwise threads (warp) with crosswise threads (weft) on a loom to make cloth.
media.history: Weaving is one of humanity's oldest crafts, and woven cloth has been central to trade and status in many societies.

media.name: Embroidery
media.description: Decorating fabric with needle and thread, using stitches to build patterns, images and text.
media.history: Embroidery appears in cultures around the world and was often used to mark rank, identity and tradition.

media.name: Quilting
media.description: Stitching layers of fabric together, often with padding in between, in decorative patterns.
media.history: Quilting began as a way to make warm bedding and clothing and grew into a rich storytelling and community art.

media.name: Macramé
media.description: Knotting cord by hand, without a loom or needle, to make patterned hangings and textures.
media.history: Knotting traditions exist in many places, and macramé became popular again in the 1900s.

media.name: Woodblock
media.description: A design is carved into a wooden block, inked, and pressed onto paper or cloth. Raised areas print.
media.history: Woodblock printing began in East Asia and later spread to Europe, where it helped make books and images affordable.
media.imageAlt: Woodblock of Collected Poems of the House of Springtime Sleep

media.name: Lithography
media.description: An image is drawn with greasy material on a flat stone or plate. Ink sticks only to the greasy areas.
media.history: Lithography was invented in the late 1700s and allowed artists to print drawings with a natural, painterly line.

media.name: Etching
media.description: Lines are bitten into a metal plate with acid. Ink fills the lines and is transferred to damp paper under pressure.
media.history: Etching became popular in Europe in the 1500s and 1600s and allowed very fine, flowing lines.

media.name: Photography
media.description: Images made by capturing light, first on chemically treated surfaces and later on digital sensors.
media.history: Photography emerged in the 1800s and quickly changed portraiture, documentation and art.
